chunks: Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the Masjid, every high thing was lowered for him and every low thing was raised for him, until he looked at Ja'far (peace be upon him) fighting the disbelievers. He said: 'Ja'far has been killed,' and a severe pain seized him in his stomach.
ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet received news of Ja'far's martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) spiritual connection to the Battle of Mu'tah, where he witnessed the martyrdom of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) through a miraculous visual phenomenon. The text emphasizes the profound physical manifestation of grief (*al-maghs*) in the Prophet's belly, underscoring the deep emotional bond between the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt. In Shia scholarship, this event is often cited to illustrate the unique status of Ja'far al-Tayyar and the shared suffering of the Prophet with his family during key historical trials.

en.hubeali: H 15012 – Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:

‘Once the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> was in the Masjid, when every high thing was lowered for him<sup>saww</sup> and every low thing was raised for him<sup>saww</sup>, to the extent that he<sup>saww</sup> saw Ja’far<sup>as</sup> fighting the infidels. He<sup>as</sup> got killed. So the Messenger<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Ja’far has been killed’, and a severe pain struck him<sup>as</sup> in his<sup>saww</sup> stomach’.
